title: Entitlement Consolidation and Audit-Proof Playbook
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook documents the standardized approach for consolidating entitlements across services, producing tamper-evident audit bundles, and aligning retention and residency metadata to satisfy regulatory and internal audit requirements. It is intended for security engineers, platform owners, SRE, and product teams operating Redwood Inference deployments (hosted, dedicated, and private).

Why this exists

- Reduce time-to-evidence for audits and incident investigations by centralizing entitlement snapshots and proofs.
- Ensure consistent retention/residency labeling so evidence complies with regulator and customer contractual obligations.
- Provide a repeatable runbook for emergency requests (forensic pulls), entitlement rollbacks, and cross-border evidence handoffs.

Scope

- Systems: Identity Broker (id-broker), Service Entitlement API (ent-api), Audit Streamer (audit-stream), Evidence Orchestrator (evidence-ctl).
- Data: role bindings, service accounts, token issuance history, attribute changes, entitlement snapshots, audit-event slices.
- Deployments: applies to Hosted API (api-redwood-prod), Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC) stacks.
- Out of scope: HR personnel records and financial ledgers (handled by Finance/legal).

Owners and escalation

- Primary owner: Security - Evidence & Controls (team: security/evidence).
- Secondary owners: Platform Identity (team: eng-infra/identity) and SRE (team: eng-sre).
- On-call escalation: security on-call -> platform identity -> legal (if PII or cross-border).

SLOs and targets

- Entitlement snapshot generation: 30m from request for standard scope (single region), 4h for cross-region consolidated bundles.
- Evidence package assembly (including signatures and residency manifests): 2h for standard, 8h cross-region.
- Immutable anchor publication to Audit Ledger: within 1 hour after package assembly.
- Goal: mean time to produce audit-ready bundle for Tier-1 customers <= 3 hours.

Standards and formats

- Snapshot format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Each record is an entitlement delta with the fields: timestamp, principal_id, resource, action, binding_id, changed_by, reason.
- Package manifest (manifest.json): top-level JSON with flat key-value fields only. Required fields: package_id, created_at (RFC3339), regions (list as CSV), retention_policy_id, residency_tags (CSV), evidence_hash (SHA256 hex), signature (base64), assembled_by, scope_description.
- Evidence packaging: TAR.GZ containing: snapshot.ndjson, manifest.json, audit-slice.ndjson (if applicable), provenance.log, kms-wrap-info.json.
- Signing: packages are signed with internal KMS key alias: projects/redwood/keys/audit-packaging-key. Signatures use RSA-PSS-SHA256 and signature blob is included in manifest.signature.

Procedure: Consolidate entitlements (normal audit)

1. Initiate request
   - Trigger: audit request ticket in JIRA (project: SEC-AUDIT) or automated periodic consolidation.
   - Gather scope: list of services, date window, tenants, and residency constraints.

2. Acquire snapshots from ent-api
   - CLI: evidence-ctl snapshot --services api-redwood-prod,ent-api,kv-cache --from 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-08-31T23:59:59Z --out /tmp/evidence/
   - ent-api returns NDJSON with per-record monotonic sequence ids.

3. Enrich with audit events
   - Pull correlated audit events from audit-stream: audit-stream export --window ... --matching-binding-ids snapshot_ids --out audit-slice.ndjson
   - Append contextual fields (request_id, trace_id) to each record.

4. Assemble package
   - evidence-ctl assemble --snapshot /tmp/evidence/snapshot.ndjson --audit /tmp/evidence/audit-slice.ndjson --out /tmp/evidence/package-<id>.tar.gz --residency us-central,eu-west --retention RP-3Y
   - The assemble step creates manifest.json and calls KMS to wrap the package key.

5. Sign and publish
   - evidence-ctl sign --package /tmp/evidence/package-<id>.tar.gz --key-alias projects/redwood/keys/audit-packaging-key
   - Publish anchor to Audit Ledger: audit-ledger publish --package /tmp/evidence/package-<id>.tar.gz --ledger-url https://ledger.redwood.internal

6. Store and index
   - Store package in Evidence Store (S3 bucket: evidence-prod) with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS). Index entry in Evidence Index service with metadata used for search and retention lifecycle.

Procedure: Emergency forensic pull (incident response)

1. Incident triage declares evidence pull needed and sets sensitivity/risk flags.
2. Security on-call creates expedited ticket with max-priority and tags customer/tenant.
3. Follow steps 'Acquire snapshots' and 'Enrich' but include live KV cache dump and short-lived debug tokens.

- Overrides: SRE may approve elevated read access for 30 minutes; all actions must be recorded.

Evidence residency and retention mapping

- Retention policy IDs (examples): RP-90D, RP-1Y, RP-3Y, RP-PERM. Map tenants to retention via customer contract metadata.
- Residency tags: us-central, eu-west, apac-sg. Packages must include residency_tags and region-specific redaction notes when data cannot leave jurisdiction.

Retention lifecycle (table)

- RP-90D: retained in evidence-prod for 90 days, auto-delete after 95 days.
- RP-1Y: retained for 1 year, snapshot archived to cold-store with 1Y+30d quarantine.
- RP-3Y: standard enterprise audit retention; packages archived to WORM storage and marked for legal hold possibility.
- RP-PERM: legal-only; manual approval to remove.

(How-to) Residency-respecting packaging

- If any record flags residency_locked = true, packaging assembly will omit full payload for non-authorized regions and include redaction markers and a minimal proof-of-presence record in the manifest.
- For cross-border export approvals, include ACL export-permit.pdf (signed) inside the package.

Evidence proofing and tamper-evidence

- Each NDJSON file is hashed per-line and the per-file Merkle root published to Audit Ledger.
- Manifest includes evidence_hash which is SHA256 of TAR.GZ content.
- Audit Ledger stores package_id, evidence_hash, published_at, and signer_key_id. Ledger entries are immutable and exposed via read-only endpoint for auditors.

Linking RBAC changes to CI/CD (secure SDLC)

- Any authorization-related PRs (changes touching ent-api or id-broker rules) must include: unit tests, a small synthetic entitlement snapshot demonstrating the change, and an evidence-manifest.yml artifact attached to the PR.
- Release gating: if PR modifies role bindings that affect Tier-1 customers, release must pass Release-Guard check: release-guard --check-role-impact.

- Developer checklist for auth changes:
  - Update ent-test-suite with new binding cases.
  - Include retrospective mapping of retention/residency for any created service accounts.
  - Add a one-paragraph explanation in the PR of how evidence packaging will look post-change.

Incident response integration

- Evidence packages created during incidents are tagged incident_id and stored in an incident-only partition (evidence-prod/incidents/<incident_id>). Access to this partition follows incident severity RBAC: only security on-call, incident lead, platform lead, and legal may access.
- After incident closure, packages are reclassified according to retention policy or quarantined for legal review.

Evidence submission to auditors and regulators

Steps to hand off:
1. Validate package manifest and ledger anchor.
2. Produce a redacted copy for external auditors, use evidence-ctl redact --policy external-audit --out /tmp/redacted.tar.gz.
3. Deliver via secure transfer: scp to auditor's secure endpoint or sFTP to audited-portal. For very sensitive cross-border transfers, use short-lived presigned URL with IP allowlist.
4. Record transfer in Evidence Index with transfer_record including transferee, date, and transfer_method.

Templates and snippets

manifest.json (example):
{
  "package_id": "pkg-20260915-73b2",
  "created_at": "2026-09-15T14:22:30Z",
  "regions": "us-central,eu-west",
  "retention_policy_id": "RP-3Y",
  "residency_tags": "us-central",
  "evidence_hash": "3f2d...fa9c",
  "signature": "MEUCIQ...==",
  "assembled_by": "evidence-ctl v2.1.0",
  "scope_description": "Monthly entitlement consolidation for August 2026 for tenant: acme-inc"
}

CLI example:
- Start snapshot: evidence-ctl snapshot --tenant acme-inc --services ent-api,id-broker,api-redwood-prod --window 2026-08-01/2026-08-31 --out /tmp/evidence/
- Assemble & sign: evidence-ctl assemble --out /tmp/evidence/pkg.tgz && evidence-ctl sign --package /tmp/evidence/pkg.tgz --key-alias projects/redwood/keys/audit-packaging-key

Operational notes and tips

- Avoid long-running package assembly on primary clusters — schedule heavy exports to off-hours or run on dedicated packaging workers.
- When residency flags block export, create a minimal proof-of-presence that includes only binding ids and hashes and embed a Redaction Map in the manifest.
- For Dedicated customers with contractual residency constraints, create per-customer packaging endpoints in their region; evidence-ctl supports region-locked mode: --region-lock eu-west.

Testing and verification

- Quarterly exercises: run a simulated audit consolidation against a non-prod mirror (mirror-evidence) and validate full end-to-end anchor to Audit Ledger.
- Test checklist:
  - Snapshot integrity: verify line counts and sequence monotonicity.
  - Manifest correctness: fields present and signature valid.
  - Ledger anchor exists and ledger endpoint returns expected hash.
  - Residency redaction: verify redaction map applied and no blocked payloads leaked.

Appendix: common error codes and remediation

- EVID-401: key wrap failure — remediation: verify KMS key alias and key rotation status; escalate to platform identity.
- EVID-422: residency-conflict — remediation: check redaction policy and request legal export permit if required.
- EVID-503: ledger-unavailable — remediation: retry with exponential backoff; if persistent, file incident with eng-sre and mark package as PENDING_ANCHOR.
